## Classification

Candidate-only preference-custody expansion for #594. This PR adds a deterministic standing-authority fixture, hash-linked authority custody, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, documentation, workflow integration, and preference-custody laboratory floor v4.

It creates no graph fact, hop, score, actor profile, real-world causal claim, preference-change finding, discrimination finding, legitimacy verdict, manipulation claim, intent inference, market-wide conclusion, or thesis evidence.

## Shared support, different authority

Every candidate world preserves the same aggregate headline:

```text
support = 800
oppose = 200
support rate = 80%
```

The authority worlds are:

```text
modeled-support-commissioner-approval
synthetic predicted support
institutional approval = true
public authorization = false

advisory-feedback-commissioner-approval
direct human advisory response
institutional approval = true
public authorization = false

binding-balanced-approval
binding affected-public disposition
alpha support = 80%
beta support = 80%
public authorization = true
implementation = authorized

binding-distributed-rejection
binding affected-public disposition
alpha support = 100%
beta support = 60%
overall support = 80%
protected group threshold fails
binding public rejection = true
implementation = blocked
```

The numeric headline remains identical. The source of evidence, the governing instrument, the rights held by affected people, and the binding consequence determine the authority class.

## Authority custody

Each world emits:

```text
proposal sealed
→ support evidence recorded
→ authority instrument sealed
→ attributed decision disposition
→ deterministic authority resolution
→ interpretation sealed
```

The instrument records the eligible constituency, quorum, overall threshold, group threshold, challenge window, and enforceable rights to amend the objective, suspend implementation, veto, appeal, and obtain remedy. The resolution records institutional approval, public authorization, binding rejection, and implementation state as separate objects.

## Refusal rules

```text
prediction = evidence, not authority
advisory feedback ≠ binding participation
institutional approval ≠ public authorization
aggregate support does not override a distributional rule
public authorization requires binding affected-public standing
objective control requires amendment, suspension, veto, appeal, and remedy
binding public rejection blocks implementation
model accuracy does not confer jurisdiction
```

## Laboratory floor v4

The aggregate floor now contains:

```text
PC-01 exposure_policy_confounding
PC-02 option_set_starvation
PC-03 observational_equivalence
PC-04 attrition_and_refusal_censoring
PC-05 subgroup_response_capacity_and_burden
PC-06 authority_laundering_and_nonbinding_consultation
```

A real case must now preserve a defined affected constituency, a binding decision rule, quorum and thresholds, objective amendment, suspension, veto, appeal, and remedy rights, an attributed constituency disposition, and an implementation receipt before public authorization can be claimed.

## Standalone qualification

The PC-06 implementation was executed before publication:

```text
node tools/compile-preference-standing.mjs
compiled same-support-different-standing-v1

node tools/validate-preference-standing.mjs
preference standing authority fixture: PASS

node test/preference-standing.test.js
preference-standing.test.js: OK
```

The focused workflow compiles, validates, tests, and preserves all six controls plus the v4 floor. The full repository release gate remains required before merge.

## Boundary

This fixture does not establish that Electric Twin, News UK, Dentsu, any vendor, any publisher, or any named institution lacks legitimacy, exceeded its authority, manipulated a public, changed preferences, or acted with improper intent. It also does not prescribe one universal constitution. Its qualified result is the separation of support evidence, institutional approval, binding public authorization, and binding public rejection under a sealed authority instrument.
head: research/preference-standing-authority-v1

Wave 31 was registered in the Wave 21 basin and generated-path contracts, rebuilt through three fixed-point passes before the complete release gate and three afterward, sharded and basin-validated, restored from the committed tree, and published with stale-head refusal. ## Classification

Candidate-only preference-custody expansion for #594. This PR adds a deterministic agenda-formation fixture, hash-linked agenda custody, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, documentation, workflow integration, and Preference Custody Laboratory Floor v5.

It creates no graph fact, hop, score, actor profile, real-world causal claim, preference-change finding, agenda-suppression finding, legitimacy verdict, manipulation claim, intent inference, market-wide conclusion, or thesis evidence.

## Shared forced choice, different agendas

The frozen population produces the same institution-authored binary result in every world:

```text
A = 800
B = 200
```

The complete synthetic rankings instead contain:

```text
C first choice = 800
A first choice = 100
NONE first choice = 100
B first choice = 0
```

A separate objective disposition records 600 people rejecting the frame itself.

The four agenda worlds are:

```text
fixed commissioner agenda
A is implemented

advisory collective proposal
C is proposed by 800 people across both affected groups
proposal has no binding amendment consequence
A is implemented

binding collective amendment
C clears overall and group petition thresholds
ballot expands to A, B, C, and NONE
C wins with 800 first choices and is implemented

binding objective challenge
60% reject the objective
implementation is blocked
```

The preliminary 80 percent support for A therefore does not identify the complete agenda, the final winner, or acceptance of the objective.

## Agenda custody

Each world emits a SHA-256 hash-linked chain:

```text
population and rankings sealed
→ initial agenda authored
→ preliminary forced choice observed
→ agenda action recorded
→ agenda authority instrument sealed
→ agenda rule resolved
→ final ballot or objective disposition recorded
→ implementation resolved
→ interpretation sealed
```

The chain preserves proposal origin, attributed coalition membership, support by group, amendment and objective-challenge thresholds, final option set, public agenda disposition, and implementation consequence.

## Executable refusal rules

```text
forced choice ≠ complete agenda
unoffered option may be collectively generated
proposal without a binding rule ≠ agenda authority
preference among offered options ≠ acceptance of the objective
preliminary winner ≠ final public disposition
collective option generation requires attributed membership and rule
synthetic prediction cannot exercise amendment rights
binding objective rejection blocks implementation
```

## Laboratory floor v5

The aggregate floor now contains:

```text
PC-01 exposure_policy_confounding
PC-02 option_set_starvation
PC-03 observational_equivalence
PC-04 attrition_and_refusal_censoring
PC-05 subgroup_response_capacity_and_burden

```

A real case must now preserve option origin, coalition formation, amendment and objective-challenge rules, preliminary and final ballots, attributed agenda disposition, and an implementation or blocking receipt before preference among institution-authored options can be narrated as the public agenda.

## Qualification plan

The focused workflow compiles, validates, tests, and preserves all seven controls plus the v5 aggregate floor. The repository release gate also runs on this PR. Merge remains blocked until both complete successfully.

## Boundary

This fixture does not establish that Electric Twin, News UK, Dentsu, any vendor, any publisher, or any named institution suppressed an option, denied an objective challenge, changed preferences, or acted with manipulative intent. It also does not prescribe one universal voting constitution. Its qualified result is the separation of preference among offered options, agenda formation, objective acceptance, and binding implementation authority.

title: Seal negotiated package formation and collective bargaining
body:
## Classification

Candidate-only preference-custody expansion for #594. This PR adds a deterministic negotiated-package fixture, hash-linked bargaining custody, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, documentation, workflow integration, and Preference Custody Laboratory Floor v6.

It creates no graph fact, hop, score, actor profile, real-world causal claim, preference-change finding, bargaining-denial finding, package-imposition finding, legitimacy verdict, manipulation claim, intent inference, market-wide conclusion, or thesis evidence.

## Fixed component poll, different packages and agreements

The frozen component poll is:

```text
X             600
Y             600
ALPHA_GUARD   400
BETA_GUARD    400
REVIEW       1000
```

A 50 percent component-majority rule selects:

```text
X + Y + REVIEW
```

Only 200 people accept that package because the two 400-person conditional cohorts require their group-specific safeguards before accepting the other group’s term.

The protected package adds both safeguards:

```text
X + Y + ALPHA_GUARD + BETA_GUARD + REVIEW
```

All 1,000 people accept it.

## Five package worlds

```text
marginal-majority bundle
20% package support
institutionally selected without collective agreement

synthetic protected candidate
100% package support
candidate only, no representative authority or agreement

advisory protected package
100% package support
institutionally approved, no binding collective agreement

binding ratified protected package
100% support in alpha and beta
mandates, reciprocity, ratification, enforcement, reopen, appeal, and remedy
collective agreement authorizes implementation

binding one-sided counteroffer
100% alpha support, 20% beta support
group threshold fails
binding bargaining impasse blocks implementation
```

## Bargaining custody

Each world emits a SHA-256 hash-linked chain:

```text
population and conditional package rules sealed
→ component poll recorded
→ versioned package proposal recorded
→ representative mandate state recorded
→ bargaining instrument sealed
→ package support and group disposition recorded
→ agreement or impasse resolved
→ implementation resolved
→ interpretation sealed
```

The chain preserves package version, conditional terms, representative mandates, reciprocal concessions, group ratification, enforceable obligations, reopen and remedy terms, agreement or impasse disposition, and implementation consequence.

## Executable refusal rules

```text
marginal clause support ≠ package acceptance
package support ≠ collective agreement
synthetic package = candidate, not bargain
advisory co-design ≠ binding collective bargaining
representative mandate requires attributed membership
negotiated package requires reciprocity, ratification, enforcement, and reopen
failed ratification = binding impasse, not missing data
package terms require versioned custody
collective agreement requires group disposition
```

## Laboratory floor v6

The aggregate floor now contains PC-01 through PC-08, adding:

```text
PC-08 negotiated_package_formation_and_collective_bargaining
```

title: Seal model, metric, policy, and validation succession
body:
## Classification

Candidate-only preference-custody expansion for #594. This PR adds a deterministic system-succession fixture, hash-linked validation custody, compiler, validator, adversarial tests, documentation, workflow integration, and Preference Custody Laboratory Floor v7.

It creates no graph fact, hop, score, actor profile, real-world causal claim, stale-validation finding, unvalidated-deployment finding, product-safety verdict, preference-change finding, manipulation claim, intent inference, market-wide conclusion, or thesis evidence.

## One public badge, six successor states

The frozen baseline is:

```text
model-v1 + prompt-v1 + retrieval-v1 + postprocess-v1
metric-v1 / one-minus-mae
policy-v1 / threshold 0.70 / select_message
benchmark-v1 / 2026-Q1
validation-v1 / score 90% / pass threshold 85%
```

Every world displays the same public headline:

```text
validated accuracy = 90%
```

The six successor states are:

```text
exact artifact and scope replay
baseline receipt remains eligible

runtime successor inherits old badge
model, prompt, and postprocessor changed
no new validation
predictive claim and deployment blocked

changed metric, current 90%, no crosswalk
current bounded result eligible
continuity with prior 90% not eligible

changed policy inherits predictive badge
predictor remains validated
new automatic-targeting policy lacks consequence test
deployment blocked

fully revalidated successor
runtime, metric, and policy changed
new validation, metric crosswalk, and policy test
bounded successor and continuity claims eligible

failed revalidation with old public badge
successor scores 75% against an 85% threshold
old badge unbound, deployment blocked, rollback required
```

## Succession custody

Each world emits a SHA-256 hash-linked chain:

```text
baseline artifact, metric, and policy sealed
→ baseline validation receipt recorded
→ successor artifact, metric, and policy sealed
→ lineage diff recorded
→ validation action and receipt state recorded
→ metric crosswalk and policy-consequence evidence recorded
→ claim eligibility resolved
→ deployment, rollback, or abstention resolved
→ interpretation sealed
```

The baseline receipt cannot overwrite the successor identity. A new score cannot overwrite the metric definition. Predictive validation cannot overwrite policy-consequence evidence. A failed revalidation cannot disappear behind a prior favorable badge.

## Executable refusal rules

```text
validation binds exact artifact, metric, policy, and scope
runtime change requires revalidation
prompt, retrieval, or postprocess change requires revalidation
metric change requires new validation and a comparability crosswalk
policy change requires consequence validation
same headline ≠ same measurement or scope
old badge cannot authorize successor
failed revalidation = negative evidence, not missing data
rollback or abstention preserves the failed result
publication claim requires current receipt and version
```

## Laboratory floor v7

The aggregate floor now contains PC-01 through PC-09, adding:

```text
PC-09 model_metric_policy_and_validation_succession
```

A real case must now preserve runtime identity and hashes, model, prompt, retrieval and postprocessing versions, benchmark and data window, metric definition and code, policy action and threshold, baseline and successor receipts, lineage diff, comparability crosswalk, policy-consequence test, public-badge scope, and rollback or abstention evidence before a historical validation can be narrated as a current successor claim.

## Qualification plan

The focused workflow compiles, validates, tests, and preserves all nine controls plus the v7 aggregate floor. The repository release gate also runs on this PR. Merge remains blocked until both complete successfully.

## Boundary

This fixture does not establish that Electric Twin, News UK, Dentsu, any vendor, any publisher, or any named institution reused stale validation, changed a system without revalidation, or deployed after a failed test. It also does not prescribe one universal validation standard. ## Classification


```text
independent private-evidence conversion

common-broadcast latent conversion
```

## Source separation

The peer-cascade world records a 50-person private seed conversion followed by 150 peer-mediated conversions through a frozen directed edge class. Removing that edge class leaves a 65/35 surface. The common-broadcast world converts the same 200 identities without any peer round. Removing the broadcast restores 60/40 while preserving the graph.

This proves the required distinction:

```text
correlated conversion
≠ peer contagion without source and temporal separation
```

## Private, public, action, and surface custody

The conformity world preserves 200 public reports that diverge from private latent preference. The coordination world preserves 200 public actions that diverge from both private preference and public report. The ranking world preserves the original 60/40 person-level state while visibility weights produce an 80/20 surfaced sample.

```text
public report ≠ private preference
public action ≠ private preference
ranked surface ≠ population report distribution
```

The existing v8 floor remains a frozen qualified base. The new v9 compiler verifies and hashes the complete v8 build, admits PC-11 separately, removes the broad network-formation frontier, adds two narrower successor frontiers, and extends the real-case promotion boundary.

body:
## Classification

Preference Custody floor v15 for issue #691. This PR adds PC-17, collective remedy enforcement, insolvency priority, successor liability, claim take-up, pass-through, provisional clawback, and durable compensation custody, as a compositional successor to the qualified v14 floor.

It creates no graph fact, hop, score, actor profile, thesis evidence, collection finding, insolvency-priority determination, successor-liability conclusion, named-organization allegation, breach or negligence finding, real-world causal effect, manipulation claim, public-authorization verdict, legitimacy finding, or inference of intent.

## Frozen remedy ledger

All eight worlds preserve:

```text
technical correction                 complete
final reference proposal             A1
public incident status               remedied
eligible affected people             100
nominal compensation obligation      2,000 units
nonmonetary correction obligation    complete
```

## Eight enforcement states

```text
segregated escrow, collective standing, complete payment, and successor guarantee
final judgment stayed pending appeal
unsecured settlement in insolvency with fractional recovery
customer indemnity without affected-party pass-through
individual-arbitration fragmentation with low take-up
successor transaction excluding remedy liability
full provisional public-fund payment subject to clawback
nonmonetary correction completed while compensation remains uncollected
```

## Deterministic separations

```text
worlds                                           8
distinct enforcement signatures                 8
distinct public-status signatures               1
complete durable collective-remedy worlds       1
appeal-stay worlds                              1
insolvency-priority-gap worlds                  2
pass-through-failure worlds                     1
claim-fragmentation worlds                      1
successor-liability-gap worlds                  2
clawback-risk worlds                            1
nonmonetary-only worlds                         1
full gross-payment worlds                       3
full gross affected-payment worlds              2
full durable-compensation worlds                1
zero durable-compensation worlds                5
collective-standing worlds                      7
total gross paid                            6,600
total gross paid to affected people         4,600
total durable compensation                   2,600
total unpaid durable obligation             13,400
maximum enforcement delay                      365 days
binding public-authority worlds                  0
```

## Positive and refusal controls

The complete world joins certified collective standing, automatic inclusion of all 100 eligible people, a final unstayed instrument, a funded and segregated trust, beneficiary protection, complete pass-through, complete durable payment, first-priority security, and a binding successor guarantee.

The negative worlds establish:

```text
judgment or settlement is not collected remedy
appeal right is not unstayed enforcement
escrow announcement is not a funded segregated account
payment to an intermediary is not payment to affected people
nominal collective eligibility is not usable collective standing
an individual claim route is not complete population remedy
gross provisional payment is not durable compensation
an insolvency claim is not priority or recovery
technical correction is not monetary restoration
a successor transaction is not liability assumption
public remedied status is not completed durable remedy
an uncollected award is not proof of breach, misconduct, or intent
```

The payment-path distinction is exact. Three worlds contain a full 2,000-unit gross payment. Two deliver that amount to affected people. Only one produces 2,000 units of durable compensation. The customer pass-through world pays the full amount into the federation and zero to affected people. The provisional public-fund world pays the full amount to affected people while preserving zero durable compensation because clawback and recoupment remain open.

## Floor v15 composition

The qualified v14 floor remains a frozen base. The v15 compiler validates and hashes the complete v14 build, admits PC-17 separately, removes the broad remedy-enforcement frontier, adds two narrower successor frontiers, and extends the real-case promotion boundary by thirty-one requirements.

```text
v14 base controls      16
PC-17 extension         1
v15 controls           17
```

The added evidence requirements cover claimant identity and contactability, collective and individual standing, representation adequacy, opt-in and opt-out state, filing burden and take-up, instrument finality, appeal and stay, escrow and security, pass-through and distribution, claim-administrator governance, insolvency priority and discharge, successor assumption, provisional payment and clawback, nonmonetary monitoring, collection and contempt, gross and durable payment, residual obligation, remedy succession, public explanation, and authority.

## Frontier transition

The broad v14 frontier:

```text
public_remedy_enforcement_insolvency_and_collective_claim_governance
```

is replaced by:

```text
collective_claim_representation_opt_out_and_distribution_governance
remedy_security_insolvency_priority_and_successor_enforcement
```

The cross-jurisdiction contribution, subrogation, and insurance-succession frontier remains open.

## Custody

Every PC-17 world emits a SHA-256 hash-linked chain:

```text
incident, correction, claimant, and nominal-remedy snapshot
→ collective standing, finality, appeal, and stay state
→ escrow, security, gross payment, pass-through, and durability state
→ insolvency, priority, distribution, discharge, and successor state
→ notice, take-up, delay, monitoring, reopen, and residual state
→ remedy-enforcement mechanism classification
→ interpretation seal
```

The compositional v15 floor emits a second chain:

```text
qualified v14 floor snapshot
→ PC-17 admission
→ remedy-enforcement frontier transition
→ remedy-enforcement real-case promotion boundary
→ interpretation seal
```

## Files

- eight-world remedy-enforcement fixture;
- compiler, validator, deterministic JSON and Markdown projections;
- per-world standing, instrument, security, payment, insolvency, succession, enforcement, residual, classification, and interpretation custody;
- focused PC-17 workflow;
- compositional v15 manifest, compiler, validator, adversarial integration test, documentation, and workflow;
- tests for claimant-population mutation, false segregation, payment inflation, clawback laundering, unpaid-ledger mutation, stay and fragmentation inflation, authority inflation, promotion-count mutation, frontier leakage, and custody tampering.

Generated projections are preserved as workflow artifacts rather than committed build products.

## Qualification

The focused PC-17 workflow, compositional Preference Custody v15 workflow, complete v14 through v9 workflows, base-floor workflow, and repository release gate all passed at the current head.

## Boundary

The admissible laboratory statement is that one complete technical correction, one public `remedied` status, one 100-person eligible population, and one 2,000-unit nominal obligation can coexist with complete payment, appeal stay, fractional insolvency recovery, pass-through failure, fragmented claims, successor exclusion, provisional clawback risk, or nonmonetary-only correction. A real enforcement claim requires complete claimant, instrument, security, payment, insolvency, succession, clawback, monitoring, residual, enforcement, and authority custody.


All eight worlds deliver notice to all 100 affected people and pay all 100 people. Four nevertheless leave part of the population without comprehension. Five preserve a meaningful-exit failure. ## Positive and refusal controls

The negative worlds establish:

```text

```

The same 95/5 disposition contains five intended exits in the qualified world and twenty in both the default and payment-first worlds. The default world generates eighty records through nonresponse. The path-cost world requires notarized mail, identification, five steps, and a 25-unit cost for exit while binding requires one login and no cost. The payment-first world exposes ninety-five people to clawback and treats retention as assent.

## Floor v20 composition

The qualified v19 floor remains a frozen base. The v20 compiler validates and hashes the complete v19 build, admits PC-22 separately, removes the broad choice-architecture frontier, adds two narrower successor frontiers, and extends the real-case promotion boundary by forty-five uniquely prefixed requirements.



## Custody

Every PC-22 world emits a SHA-256 hash-linked chain:

```text

→ intention, attempt, completion, failure, abandonment, and authorship
→ explicit, inferred, representative, default, and bundled assent

```

```text

```

The permanent PR surface contains exactly fourteen files: the eight-world fixture; standalone compiler, validator, tests, documentation, and focused workflow; and the compositional v20 manifest, compiler, validator, integration test, documentation, and workflow. Generated JSON and Markdown projections remain workflow artifacts rather than committed build products.

## Boundary

The admissible laboratory statement is that verified comprehension, one operative release, one public `choice_final` status, one recorded 95-bound/5-exited disposition, and full payment can coexist with neutral active choice, binding default, asymmetric exit cost, urgency, repeated confirmation, bundled assent, representative substitution, or payment-first clawback. title: Complete PC-45 interval construction, dependence, multiplicity, and empirical coverage custody
body:
Closes #978.

## Classification

Preference Custody **PC-45: linkage-interval target, construction, out-of-sample design, data separation, dependence, resampling, effective sample size, multiplicity, adaptive selection, simultaneous coverage, empirical denominator, correction, and lineage custody**.

This PR composes the qualified forty-four-control floor-v42 base with one standalone eight-world control and publishes Preference Custody laboratory floor v43.

It creates no real identity map, interval, empirical coverage estimate, target-population or subgroup burden, causal effect, longitudinal history, named-person or named-institution finding, graph fact, thesis-evidence claim, consequential-use authorization, public-authority verdict, coordination finding, common-purpose finding, or inference of intent.

## Frozen public interval surface

All eight worlds preserve:

```text
operative release                       RELEASE-INCIDENT-V1@1

published candidate pairs             100
published interval-bearing pairs      100
published nominal coverage             95%
published empirical coverage           95%
published interval misses                5

```

The worlds distinguish complete assurance from an undefined or mismatched target; in-sample construction and calibration-validation reuse; entity, source, cluster, or temporal leakage; invalid pair-level resampling and overstated effective sample size; uncorrected multiplicity and adaptive selection; selective empirical denominators that omit hard negatives or unlabelled pairs; and stale inherited lineage.

title: Reject non-canonical and cross-root-aliased v45 inputs before PC-48 cache reuse
body:
Follow-up to merged PR #1083 and its final PC-48 cache-review findings.

## Defect

`validateQualifiedV45Base` cached clean v45 validation by a JSON-derived hash. Serialization-ambiguous mutations could collide with a qualified cache key, and the first recursive repair still tracked object identity separately for `baseBuild` and `baseSources`. An equal-content subtree aliased across those roots could therefore evade repeated-identity refusal and reuse a warmed success.

## Repair

- exact-key validation uses `Reflect.ownKeys`, refusing symbol and non-enumerable additions as well as ordinary enumerable additions;
- recursive cache admission permits only canonical plain JSON trees: null, strings, booleans, finite numbers, plain objects, and dense canonical arrays;
- unsupported values, custom prototypes, accessors, non-enumerable properties, symbol keys, sparse or extra-key arrays, repeated identity, and cycles are refused before hashing;
- one shared `WeakSet` validates the complete live `baseBuild` + `baseSources` graph, so identities shared across cache roots are refused;
- a separate shared identity ledger validates the complete structured-clone snapshot graph;
- the cache key is derived from the qualified snapshot, and the live digest must equal the snapshot digest before lookup and after full v45 validation;
- transitive source-bundle key diagnostics and direct chronology diagnostics remain ahead of full v45 validation;
- compile-time and compiled-build validation both preflight before source hashing, chronology hashing, or cache reuse.

title: Topology: compile the actor-hop admission frontier
body:
This transaction is a topology-admission and denominator-governance correction for the public surface-hop graph. The governed objects are canonical surfaces, actor and organization participation rows, compiled actor-pair bases, explicit surface refusals, and temporal pair refusals. The acting components are the topology compiler and the standing release workflow.

The compiler now classifies every canonical surface as admitted, explicitly refused, singleton context, zero-actor context, or an invalid ungoverned multi-actor non-hop surface. A hop-eligible surface must contain at least two distinct actors, give every admitted actor at least one receipted participation row, and account for every unordered actor pair on that exact surface. A pair satisfies that denominator only when it appears as a compiled basis or as an explicit `rejected_hop_pairs` record produced by disjoint dated participation windows. A temporal refusal remains visible and countable, but it is not converted into an edge.

Every non-hop surface containing two or more distinct actors must publish a non-empty `hop_refusal_reason`. These changes govern existing source-supported context; they do not admit or remove an actor, receipt, participation, claim, edge, or public route.

The compiler writes `build/topology-admission-frontier.json` during the normal compile. The artifact enumerates admitted surfaces, explicit refusals, unrefused context-only surfaces, compiled pair bases, temporally refused pairs, and any missing pair denominator. Organization participation remains visible context, but an organization identifier in `actor_a` or `actor_b` is a release error and cannot satisfy an actor-pair denominator.

The mutation suite exercises an unrefused multi-actor directory, a missing pair with neither a basis nor a temporal refusal, an unreceipted actor participation, an organization endpoint, a singleton surface incorrectly marked hop eligible, and a valid temporal refusal that must remain graph-inert without failing denominator completeness. The evidence tier is canonical ledger state, compiled hop bases and temporal pair refusals, executable mutations, and the full repository release gate. The venue is this pull request and the generated topology-admission frontier. The target is denominator completeness and refusal governance, rather than any substantive relationship claim. title: CI: fix research fan-out matrix output quoting
body:

title: CI: harden research fan-out issue reconciliation
body:
## What changed

This change hardens the production research fan-out workflow at the durable issue boundary. The dispatch step now enumerates the complete open issue ledger through explicit REST pagination, ignores pull requests that share an issue title, and refuses to mutate repository state when more than one open issue has the exact batch title. The workflow also adds a terminal audit job that compares every current manifest batch with exactly one open issue, verifies the embedded fingerprint and complete body, computes a deterministic corpus digest, and retains a machine-readable reconciliation receipt.

## Root cause and mechanism

The previous dispatch path used `gh issue list --limit 200` and selected the first exact-title match. Once the repository exceeded that bounded projection, a valid existing issue could fall outside the lookup window, and duplicate exact titles would be silently reduced to the first result. The production run itself is complete and correct, but that lookup mechanism did not provide a durable rerun guarantee. The replacement uses the REST issue ledger rather than GitHub search indexing, which was separately observed to return a false duplicate/missing projection during verification even though the canonical REST records were exact.

The post-dispatch audit runs after all matrix cells settle, including failure cases. It fails when dispatch did not succeed, when a current batch is missing or duplicated, when a fingerprint differs, when a body differs, or when the current expected and actual corpus digests diverge. Historical open fan-out titles outside the current manifest remain visible in the receipt without blocking a valid current run.

## Production evidence

Canonical production run `31814310465` executed commit `f20fb65c3dce9801b0b4490eb68f3b0ba7906c56` successfully. Its archived artifact `9224369948` contains 1,409 tasks across 137 batches and 137 matrix entries. A complete REST reconciliation found one prepare job, 137 successful dispatch jobs, and 137 consecutive open issues from #1987 through #2123. Every issue title, fingerprint, and body matched the archived packet corpus. The expected and actual corpus digests were identical: `aee4feb255a81b7d743aa7a8c90c6e56177925c502c275882a83ff06a9ec040a`.

## Validation

Validation run `31825652780` checked the exact committed workflow blob `992dab5c4627c65099c9029ff14f20ce2cb76381`. It executed the committed dispatch block against paginated fixtures and proved that an exact issue beyond the former 200-record boundary is edited, a same-title pull request is ignored, duplicate exact issue titles are rejected before mutation, and no-match behavior creates the exact requested title.

The same run executed the committed audit blocks against the live production artifact and complete REST issue ledger. The baseline reconciled all 137 batches with the production corpus digest. Mutation controls then proved that a missing expected issue, a duplicate expected title, and body divergence are rejected, while an unrelated historical fan-out title is accepted and reported. The disposable validation branch was deleted only after its exact head and parent SHAs were verified.

After `main` advanced, the candidate was rebuilt as commit `bf441662519edd70bc1026e72ec219434e0c8e64` with current canonical parent `5bf9a4b4ea4eecfc957f517e298d0997d52dd58c`. The upstream workflow blob remained unchanged, and the rebased candidate retains the exact validated workflow blob. The pull request is therefore one commit and one changed file without overwriting intervening repository changes.

## Scope

The pull request changes only `.github/workflows/research-fanout.yml`. It did not dispatch the production workflow, create or edit any research issue, or modify generated research data.

title: Fix Pages retries with attempt-scoped artifacts
body:
The first deployment attempt for run 32055169795 completed the full release check and uploaded the Pages artifact, then GitHub returned a server-side 503 while creating the deployment. This change assigns `github-pages-${{ github.run_attempt }}` to `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` and passes the same value through `artifact_name` to `actions/deploy-pages@v4`. The two official actions expose those inputs, so the deployment remains bound to the current attempt while prior-attempt artifacts cannot create an ambiguous selection.

title: [Crawler] Harden Dentsu redaction and bounded feed reads
body:
## Summary

This pull request hardens the governed first-party industrial-exhaust lane over six official Dentsu English and Japanese feeds. The crawler captures the bounded publication surface into immutable, non-canonical evidence receipts. Watch terms prioritize review but do not filter ingestion.

## Governance boundary

Every enabled observation remains an attributable `first_party_corporate_publication` with `graph_effect: none`, `promotion_authority: false`, and `canonical_mutation_authorized: false`. This lane cannot create actors, relationships, adjudicated claims, scores, cases, or canonical graph mutations.

## Contact-boundary hardening

Telephone detection uses bounded NFKC-normalized digit-group windows while preserving original narrative characters. International handling covers ASCII and fullwidth plus signs, generic `00`, North American `011`, Japanese `010`, and Australian `0011` access prefixes. Domestic handling covers compact Japanese geographic and service numbers, two- and three-group forms, four-to-six pair-group forms, compact Japanese labels, North American grouping, and parenthesized forms.

The redaction callback locates the first actual phone marker or digit inside every regex match and checks adjacency at that true contact offset. Leading whitespace can no longer suppress phones after prose, while letter-attached identifiers remain protected.

Dotted contact continuation receives the contextual tail and yields to parenthesized narrative evidence. The phone and marked-extension observation scanners also examine sentence punctuation without requiring intervening whitespace, preserving both ASCII `. (00) attendees` and fullwidth `．（００） attendees` while retaining a no-narrative parenthesized contact-format control.

## URL, identifier, and streaming preservation

Numeric paths in explicit, scheme-relative, bare-domain, punycode, and IPv4 URLs remain intact. Dates, metrics, GUIDs, release identifiers, revisions, and phone-shaped non-contact identifiers remain outside contact redaction unless a later span independently qualifies as a phone.

Accepted response bodies are decoded incrementally as UTF-8. The crawler rejects on the first byte-limit crossing chunk, cancels the reader, releases the lock, and does not request unread trailing chunks.

## Exact-head receipts

Exact reviewed PR head: `0ce287d9d9f15b809c48bc1a6e6aa43a8c1fe6d6`.

Implementation commit: `6c0e19dd8aa480aa8d7c5014be808c0a98565790`.

- `tools/crawl-industrial-exhaust.mjs`: `22c4cc8a53058bbb128d064850c2a7c71a4367de`

Exact-head GitHub Actions completed successfully:

- First-party industrial-exhaust intake #163, run `32212100841`
- No magic human gate #3577, run `32212100854`
- Release checks #6170, run `32212100827`

The focused suite covers separated domestic phones after prose, attached-identifier controls, ASCII and fullwidth parenthesized narrative after phone and extension spans, no-narrative parenthesized contact formatting, compact and grouped domestic numbers, international access prefixes, URL and identifier preservation, signed numeric prose, split UTF-8 code points, immediate byte-limit rejection, cancellation, lock release, and unread-tail protection.

All inline review threads are resolved at the exact reviewed head.

## Evidentiary boundary

Evidence tier: first-party attributable publication. Venue: six English and Japanese RSS surfaces. Target: the rolling publication stream. Upside: replayable discovery of product, partnership, data, governance, personnel, and capital events. Downside: publisher control over framing and feed retention. title: Fix industrial-exhaust alert rematching and hydration rotation
body:
This follow-up addresses the two actionable P2 review findings posted after #2168 merged. The affected object is the bounded first-party industrial-exhaust artifact hydrator. The relevant actors are the scheduled crawler, repository maintainers, and the current watch-term registry that determines which publisher artifacts remain in the review queue.

The first defect allowed `buildArtifactAlerts` to reuse an artifact’s historical `seed_matched_terms` when the current candidate set no longer contained that URL. A removed or renamed watch term could therefore survive as a queued alert even though neither the current feed or index routing surface nor the hydrated body matched the current registry. The fix treats current-registry rematching as authoritative: when `watchConfig` is supplied, seed matches come only from the current candidate; historical seed terms remain available solely for explicit replay without a current registry.

The second defect used a fixed original position within each hydration state rank. Under the scheduled `--limit=50` run, successful or failed cohorts larger than the limit could permanently starve their tails. The fix preserves the existing priority order of unseen pages, prior errors, and prior successes, then selects the least recently checked pages within each rank using `last_checked_at`, with the original candidate position retained only as a deterministic tie-breaker.

Regression coverage proves that a retired historical seed cannot create a current alert, that historical replay remains available without a current registry, and that both successful and failed cohorts rotate toward their least recently checked members. The dedicated artifact suite, JavaScript syntax checks, whitespace validation, and the repository-wide release gate pass in the branch materializer. The patch changes only `tools/lib/industrial-exhaust-artifacts.mjs` and `test/industrial-exhaust-artifacts.test.js`; it does not change evidence class, graph effect, promotion authority, canonical mutation authority, source allowlists, or acquisition scope.

The resulting map keeps publisher artifacts revision-aware while making registry changes and bounded scheduling operationally honest. The control question is whether every currently relevant candidate can be revisited under a finite run limit without preserving obsolete watch terms or indefinitely starving the tail of a state cohort.

## Summary

This post-merge hardening follow-up corrects a narrative-normalization defect left after #2176. The merged implementation applied explicit identifier-context protection only inside the compact-domestic classifier. Grouped domestic, parenthesized, North American, and international phone-shaped identifiers could therefore bypass the guard, while standalone `ID` and fullwidth `ＩＤ` labels were not recognized.

The corrected implementation normalizes the prefix once, recognizes the existing English and Japanese identifier labels plus standalone `ID`, and applies the guard before any phone-candidate class receives an affirmative score. An affirmative phone label retains precedence. The repair is limited to `tools/lib/industrial-exhaust.mjs` and `test/industrial-exhaust.test.js`.

## Failure and repair

Before the repair, identifier-labelled values such as `GUID: 03-6216-8041`, `reference: +81 3 6216 5111`, `管理番号：03-6216-8041`, and `識別子：+81 3 6216 5111` could be rewritten as `[contact omitted]`, even though they were identifiers rather than narrative contact disclosures. `ID: 09012345678` had no explicit identifier protection.

The repair computes one NFKC-normalized prefix, evaluates URL context and identifier context against that prefix, and returns a zero phone score when an explicit identifier label is present without an affirmative telephone label. This gate now precedes compact, grouped, parenthesized, North American, and international scoring. Recursive scanning remains active, so protecting an identifier does not suppress a later independently labelled phone.

Regression coverage proves that ASCII and fullwidth `ID`, grouped English identifiers, international English identifiers, grouped Japanese identifiers, and international Japanese identifiers remain intact. title: [Crawler] Reset abbreviation-led sentence boundaries
body:
## Problem

The narrative-period classifier must distinguish a recognized abbreviation that continues into an institutional title from one that ends a sentence before a telephone span. A false continuation drops a legitimately owned wrapper closer, while a false boundary carries an ownerless closer across ordinary prose.

## Repair

The candidate applies ordered grammatical, casing, suffix, and terminal-label evidence after recognized narrative abbreviations. It preserves title-shaped continuations including `U.S. I Corps`, `U.S. IT Department`, `Acme Inc. We Care Center`, `U.S. We the People Foundation`, `U.S. She Leads Africa`, `U.S. This Is Us Foundation`, `It's a Small World Foundation`, and `We Can Do It Foundation`. Straight, curly, and compatibility-normalized contractions are recognized. Terminal labels accept `number`, `no.`, `#`, compatibility-normalized fullwidth forms, and common title-to-label separators such as hyphens, dashes, pipes, slashes, and backslashes.

Institutional suffixes and title casing are affirmative evidence, but neither is conclusive when stronger clause structure is present. The classifier recognizes bounded predicates, constrained regular past and third-person forms, plural-subject base forms after `we`, `you`, `they`, `these`, and `those`, and title-case pronoun clauses containing a finite predicate, object determiner, and substantive object. It therefore resets ownership for `HE VISITED THE COMPANY`, `THEY PURCHASE TICKETS`, `WE ACQUIRE ASSETS`, `YOU PURCHASE THE TICKETS`, `He Visited The Company`, and `She Leads The Foundation`. Labelled title-shaped institutions and unlabelled mixed-case organization names remain protected, including `He Visited The Company Phone:`, `THEY PURCHASE TICKETS FOUNDATION Phone:`, `She Leads Africa`, and `This Is Us Foundation`.

The final repair bounds three ambiguous mechanisms. A plural-base guess may defeat a terminal institutional suffix only when it has determiner-object evidence or a compact two-token named object, so `WE INSPIRE YOUNG PEOPLE FOUNDATION` remains a title while `THEY VISIT ACME FOUNDATION` remains a clause. A title-cased copular phrase with an object marker, at least two substantive title tokens, and a terminal institutional suffix remains entity evidence, preserving `We Are The World Foundation` while non-copular clauses continue to reset ownership. Orthographic `-ing` is no longer treated as conclusive participial morphology: a bounded lexical set admits inherent base verbs such as `bring`, `sing`, `swing`, `spring`, and `string`, while productive non-finite forms remain excluded.

The product diff is confined to:

- `tools/lib/industrial-exhaust.mjs`
- `test/industrial-exhaust.test.js`

## Qualification

The current owner-authored head is `8543858faf820bb8f11c6d3058066d94377b7843`, directly parented by live `main` at `dae4917b16a4e08450ee79a1ad33ab4f3d3416cd`, with tree `ba0c65925c9f0c4b7f69869ebc168946ca921f8d`. The pull request contains one commit and exactly two changed files.

Direct ASCII and fullwidth regressions cover the reported suffix-title, copular-title, and lexical-`ing` mechanisms alongside the prior pronoun, predicate, casing, contraction, label, separator, and compatibility-normalization matrix. Every review thread carries an exact-head disposition and is resolved.

Venue: follow-up to merged PR #2194. Target: abbreviation-led wrapper ownership before telephone redaction. title: [CI] Fetch PR head history without assuming an origin branch
body:

Missing pull-head refs, missing stable base refs, transport or authentication failures, unresolved `HEAD`, failed exact-SHA acquisition, and a repository that remains shallow continue to fail closed.

The regression suite models a fork head branch and a deleted same-repository head branch, proves that neither produces an origin branch refspec, and verifies that the pull-head ref supplies the contributor-history anchor. title: [Transport] Publish industrial-exhaust revision-occurrence repair
body:
This draft pull request is a transport-only controller and must not be merged. The product actors are the RSS observation ledger, sitemap-discovery ledger, hydrated-artifact ledger, and their append-only revision chains. The controller actor is this isolated workflow on `agent/industrial-exhaust-revision-occurrence-controller-v1`. The intended product branch is `agent/industrial-exhaust-revision-occurrence-v1`, reconstructed from exact canonical base `cdc9d3670fb226e92ff90952c3f8a4392c532a26`.

The defect is an occurrence-identity collision. The three merge functions currently derive `observation_id`, `discovery_id`, and `artifact_id` from stable record identity plus the current content digest. That identifies a content state, but it does not identify the position of that state in a revision chain. Under A → B → A, the later A receives the first A identifier while carrying `revision_number: 3` and `revision_of` pointing to B. Under A → B → A → B, both content states reuse earlier identifiers. The result is a non-injective append-only lineage in which distinct revision occurrences can claim the same primary ID.

The controller inserts a predecessor-bound occurrence-ID function while preserving the existing initial-record namespace. A first occurrence retains the current stable-record-plus-content derivation. Every later occurrence additionally binds the immediate predecessor ID. Equal content therefore retains an equal content or projection digest, while recurrence after an intervening revision receives a new occurrence ID. The repair covers feed observations, sitemap discoveries, and hydrated artifacts rather than leaving the base RSS lane with the same defect.

The regression matrix exercises A → B → A and A → B → A → B for all three ledgers. It requires equal recurring content digests, unique occurrence identifiers, exact immediate-predecessor `revision_of` links, monotonically increasing revision numbers, unchanged-entry deduplication, and four unique IDs across four occurrences. title: Fix: make industrial-exhaust receipt publication no-overwrite

title: Fix: make industrial-exhaust receipt publication crash-durable
body:
This pull request closes the crash-durability boundary left by the no-overwrite receipt publisher. The current writer synchronizes the complete private temporary file, but it does not synchronize the directory entries that make the content-addressed receipt reachable. A successful return can therefore precede durable persistence of a newly created directory or final receipt name.

The repair creates missing receipt-directory components one at a time, verifies that each component is a real directory, and synchronizes both the component and its parent. After hard-link publication and private-temporary cleanup, it synchronizes the final receipt directory before returning. The same synchronization proof is required when an existing receipt is reused, so a retry after an uncertain prior publication cannot silently upgrade an unsynchronized entry to success.

The regression covers index and artifact receipts. It verifies that every directory in a newly created receipt path is synchronized, that a directory synchronization occurs after the final hard link, that idempotent reuse preserves bytes while synchronizing the retained directory, and that an injected directory-sync failure causes the writer to fail closed.

title: NEVER MERGE: qualify PR #2231 complete observation and extension custody v86
body:
This draft pull request is disposable execution custody for product PR #2231 and must never merge. Its single workflow-only commit `073f0817e0d41acd59b16437cc69ee10ef578428` is directly parented to frozen `main@564da53a373bfee43b026d7ed0ba0022bcc38633`, with tree `d3b00d4c5fc764a361d2510ec1a0e2f90f5a30aa`, workflow blob `a009e4ecb588ce8409451e758c6c0c9f5203afce`, one commit, and exactly `.github/workflows/temporary-pr2231-complete-observation-extension-controller-v86.yml`. The workflow decodes only the SHA-256-bound execution payload retained below. No controller path may enter product history.

The controlled object is exclusive source custody among short-year dotted dates, complete attached observations, phone-shaped unit observations, and extension-bearing telephone intervals on exact product head `932089e4911d96cf27997dc39bed15c4e00e1570`. The actors are `intrinsicPhoneContinuationLimit`, `completeIntrinsicPhoneContinuation`, `crossCallbackObservationMatch`, `validatedIntrinsicPhoneInterval`, the mutable observation endpoint in `independentPhoneStartAfterObservation`, generic interval optimization, `PHONE_EXTENSION_PATTERN`, and exact range rendering.

Fresh exact-head review proves two current product defects after the v84 grouped-observation repair. First, `Archive 3.12.03/20-08-17` and the period, dash, and fullwidth equivalents can still combine a short-year group with an attached complete date into one synthetic telephone interval. Second, `Archive 2026-08-17 03-62165111 people` loses only the phone-shaped numeric prefix because ordinary post-observation precedence returns an intrinsic interval before the callback-aware matcher can claim the complete external unit. A separate v85 controller, PR #2384, also identified extension-bearing contacts such as `Archive 3.12.03-6216-8041 ext 55`; its run `33148434205`, job `98774602798`, failed closed at an invalid synthetic runtime assertion before repository qualification, and the product ref did not move. This controller supersedes that failed execution object without amending or rebasing it.

V86 composes the three mechanisms. Complete attached dates and unit-bearing observations terminate the short-year continuation scan before synthetic telephone construction, while exact dotted telephone groups remain eligible. Ordinary post-observation precedence computes the complete callback-aware observation and source endpoint before allowing an intrinsic prefix to win; a phone-shaped prefix cannot preempt an externally owned unit. When a leading strong observation and every subsequent complete observation own the remainder and no later telephone validates, the function returns terminally rather than falling through to an optimizer that lacks those observation ranges. Extension evidence never creates telephone authority: one complete context-free telephone interval must validate first, after which an explicit `ext`, `extension`, `x`, `#`, `＃`, or `内線` marker may terminate the continuation proof and the existing extension pass removes the extension digits.

The deterministic payload reconstructs exact repair script blob `e7bb3d9b47d763c7d3baa28d6cbbd99d2e943bf3` in the Actions workspace, starts from product tree `e377e456efbc64b858bc85765dabd7b0e53e4aa0` and blobs `4ea5698df5928ad51c42172057578c0c2ef1781a` and `9a5ce8776697ae36d9833c052bfa923cf43f210d`, and requires candidate blobs `54c390839fa06f39b83e3fd2cac9852082bc9a09` and `6941d9bedc20b3a83a4f2ce96bfbf79457def077`. Local exact-head replay reproduced the attached-date, unit-observation, and extension failures; passed the cumulative focused suite; retained the original `Archive 3.12.03 62-16 20 people` control; passed ASCII and fullwidth dates, units, domestic, mobile, dotted, invalid-closer, sentence-expiry, and one-use-lease controls; and processed 750 extension-bearing contacts with exactly 1,500 omissions under the bounded runtime gate.

Hosted execution must revalidate the controller, main, product, tree, blob, count, and path leases; reproduce every predecessor failure before mutation; apply only `tools/lib/industrial-exhaust.mjs` and `test/industrial-exhaust.test.js`; run every `industrial-exhaust*.test.js` suite on repaired product bytes and the frozen-main transplant; complete `npm run release:check`; restore generated state; construct one owner-authored two-file commit over frozen main; revalidate every live lease; and publish only through exact `force-with-lease`. PR #2231 remains draft and unmerged. No review thread is resolved by this controller, and PR #2227 remains untouched.

Evidence tier: fresh exact-head P1 and P2 review findings, deterministic predecessor reproduction, content-addressed workflow and repair objects, cumulative focused execution, and pending hosted current-main and repository-wide qualification. Venue: unresolved PR #2231 review threads, failed-closed controller PR #2384, this never-merge controller, GitHub Actions, and the retained artifact. Target: complete observation and telephone interval custody at the three overlapping precedence seams. Upside: complete observations remain byte-for-byte intact while every independently complete extension-bearing or later telephone reaches rendering with its exact interval. Downside: eligible transitions perform bounded complete-observation and extension-marker checks. Failure mode: a synthetic telephone crosses an observation, a phone-shaped prefix steals an external unit, a valid extension-bearing telephone remains exposed, an observation suppresses a disjoint phone, a stale ref publishes, or any second controller path or third product path enters the result.

Does the hosted receipt prove that complete attached and unit-bearing observations retain exclusive source custody, every extension-bearing successor begins with an independently validated telephone interval, and the exact one-commit two-file product is published without renewing a lease, resolving a thread, promoting PR #2231, or modifying any quarantined history?

The existing mechanism counted rows with an exact amount and rows containing any sufficiently long programme token, then declared the summary verified when both populations were nonempty. The matching amount and programme could therefore belong to different awards. A generic word such as “manufacturing” could satisfy the programme side, and exact dollar equality could reject a correctly rounded headline while numeric coercion could treat invalid values too generously. No current saved lead was falsely admitted because all five stored verification flags remain false, but the decision rule contained a reproducible false-positive path.

The repair preserves the legacy counts as discovery diagnostics, adds a same-row diagnostic, validates input shape and finite numeric values, and fixes `trade_summary_exactly_verified` at false for this search surface. The output now states `not_verified_by_award_search` and records the missing predicates: source-native recipient identity, awarding agency, signed transaction dates, complete transaction coverage, and an explicit amount-precision rule. Even a same-row award total remains insufficient to establish fiscal-year action obligations. This change narrows the classifier without discarding returned official rows or pretending that the existing search endpoint answers a transaction-level question.

Eight synthetic regressions cover split-row matches, a same-row match, generic programme language, rounded amounts, null, blank, Boolean, nonnumeric and infinite values, duplicated and empty populations, malformed inputs, and the unchanged five-lead manifest. Native qualification on OCTO-N01 used Node `v24.19.0`, `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, and the complete `npm run release:check`, all successful on the current exact tree. The current-base release completed in 48.968 seconds; stdout SHA-256 is `6eaefef0092c4c905a6e16256d37faa2360f819d21287e4cf93cec82a8739daa`, and stderr is empty. The wider evidence map remains unchanged. This software repair neither resolves that disagreement nor publishes a fiscal claim. ## Purpose

PR #2626 reproduces the remaining unattended-admission defect on the current protected `main`: the scheduled crawler produced a direct-child candidate, the explicitly dispatched Release and No-magic workflows succeeded on the exact candidate SHA, and the native `pull_request` workflows terminated `action_required` because `github-actions[bot]` created the pull request with `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

It does not weaken branch protection, grant a bypass, alter the two required contexts, or let the publisher App manufacture checks.

## Bounded change

The implementation is complete only after a fresh scheduled source mutation creates an App-authored crawler PR, native Release and No-magic workflows start without human approval, both app-bound required checks pass on the exact candidate, the ordinary protected merge endpoint admits it, topology verification succeeds, and the candidate branch retires.
